summary: Leaf 41 is also a seki in Black's sente. The seki already held after White's D16, Black's A16 was a free forcing move that White had to answer at A17, and Black can now play elsewhere. White keeps one forcing move, A14 (capturing two stones), which Black answers with the throw-in at A15. White's fill at C17 or A19 loses to Black's D19. As with leaf 34, the label turns on question 6: S[SEKI+] if you want the + for a seki in the solver's sente, S[SEKI] if trees without the + keep it. Its sibling leaf 42 (D16 instead of A15 at move 9) is also a seki in Black's sente, because the A15 that Black still owes there is sente, but the checker prints SEKI there because its test only lets the solver pass.
variations: From leaf 41, Black to play. (1) pass: seki. White to play cannot live, and Black cannot improve if White also passes (checker SEKI). (2) pass C17 D19: White's fill is self-atari, and D19 captures the group (DEAD). (3) pass A19 D19: D19 captures A19-B19-C19 and the rest dies (DEAD). (4) pass A14 A15: White's one forcing move and Black's throw-in answer; the seki holds (White to play: SEKI). pass A14 A15 A16: Black may play elsewhere again (SEKI+). (5) pass A14 A13: the wrong answer; White's A15 makes an eye and lives (ALIVE). pass A14 pass: White's A15 lives too (ALIVE). (6) pass F19: Black can ignore it (SEKI+). (7) A19 C17, or C17 A19: Black's own fill gives White four stones and life (ALIVE). (8) F19 D19: Black's forcing move; the seki stays (SEKI+). (9) Before the leaf, after White's D16: the position is already SEKI+, and A16 pass A17 is DEAD, so A16 A17 was Black's free forcing exchange. (10) Sibling leaf 42 (B18 B19 C18 C19 D19 E19 A18 B17 D16 C17): if Black passes, White's A15 lives. After Black's A15, every White move except A16 is DEAD, and after A15 A16 Black may play elsewhere (SEKI+).

depends_on: Question 6 (SEKI+ and SEKI) and its rider on trees that use no +. 13547 never uses the +. If the answer is 'SEKI+: the solver keeps sente', the leaf is S[SEKI+], because Black may play elsewhere and White's A14 is only White's own forcing move. If it is 'SEKI+ only with the solver to play', it is also S[SEKI+], since White's A17 is the last move. If it is 'no + from the checker', or the + only in trees that already use it, S[SEKI] stands. If he wants the +, leaf 42 should get it too: Black's owed A15 is sente and White's only answer is A16. The checker cannot see this, because its test allows the solver a pass but not a forcing move first.
earlier_research: The question-6 census, run before the group F fix, listed this leaf as 'SEKI or SEKI+ (sente test undecided)'; the fix decides it as SEKI+. Leaf 42, undecided in that census, is now SEKI by the one-pass test. Yet a forcing move (A15, answered only at A16) followed by a pass keeps Black's sente there. So leaf 42 is a leaf where the page's two sente tests differ, unlike the 128 leaves on which the page found both tests decided and in agreement. No earlier round judged leaf 41. The ko verdicts on 13547 (k041 to k044 and k104) are untouched.
